discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 231930
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
230 PM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Seasonal temperatures this week with highs in the 40s.

- There is a 20% chance of rain showers this evening, mainly 
  for northern areas. Snow may briefly mix in late. 

- 60% to 80% chance of rain on Thanksgiving. Snowflakes may mix
  in later Thursday night.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 208 PM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

A cold northwest flow shortwave will cross over Lake Michigan 
this evening. Lake enhanced showers are already developing
across Michigan and are expected to move into the local forecast
area in the next few hours. Precipitation will mainly be north
of the Toll Road and fall as light rain. However, as
temperatures drop overnight, some snow could mix in. Winds will
also back from northwest to north and then northeast, shifting
showers back towards northwest Indiana before they taper off
Tuesday morning. Little to no snow accumulation is forecast
given shallow moisture profiles.

High pressure will build back in for Tuesday for dry conditions
with highs in the upper 30s to low 40s. The upper level flow
will become southerly on Wednesday, and it will warm slightly
into the mid 40s. The next weather system will also start moving
up into the region on Wednesday, bringing rain into the 
southwest. Some snow could also mix in on Wednesday night west 
of I-69, but amounts will be minimal. Rain will then overspread 
the area on Thanksgiving, with a chance for snow showers again 
Thursday night into Friday morning. Confidence is low that there
will be any accumulations since surface temperatures will 
generally remain above freezing. Showers will diminish on Friday
as the moves into New England. DRier conditions can be expected
Saturday and Sunday, although a series of weaker shortwaves 
could bring light precip at times.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 1115 AM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

Cyclonic, northwest flow continues with low end VFR. Scattered
light rain/snow showers are expected in the vicinity of Lake 
Michigan between 0-6Z tonight as vort max moves through the 
area. No accumulation expected but have added a PROB30 at KSBN
to account for this potential. Have kept KFWA dry due to dry air
away from the lake. Low end VFR ceilings persist through the TAF
forecast period; peak cloud cover is expected to be downwind of
Lake Michigan. Northwest winds continue today with a few gusts 
to 20 kts possible prior to sunset. Overnight, winds become 
light and variable.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 7 AM EST Tuesday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Cobb
AVIATION...Johnson

spc.text:
SPC AC 231934

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0134 PM CST Mon Nov 23 2026

   Valid 232000Z - 241200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected through tonight.

   ...20Z Update...
   Minimal changes were made to the Day 1 Convective Outlook. Thunder
   probabilities were trimmed in CO, where a prevalence in freezing
   temperatures will reduce liquid/ice phase mixing and subsequent
   efficient lightning generation, though a couple of flashes remain
   possible. Sparse lightning flashes may also occur with any
   appreciable updraft that becomes sustained over central NC, given
   buoyancy topping at around -10 C in altitude per latest RAP forecast
   soundings. However, such scant buoyancy suggests any lightning that
   develops will be too isolated to warrant thunder probabilities.

   ..Squitieri.. 11/23/2026

   .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1022 AM CST Mon Nov 23 2026/

   ...Central/Southern Rockies and Southern High Plains...
   Large-scale forcing for ascent accompanying a midlevel trough moving
   across the Great Basin will overspread a cold air mass over the
   central Rockies today. Steepening lapse rates/weak instability may
   support isolated lightning flashes with any convective elements.
   Related forcing for ascent will impinge on the southern Rockies and
   adjacent High Plains tonight, where elevated thunderstorms will also
   be possible. 

   ...Central Gulf Coast...
   Isolated thunderstorms are possible along/ahead of a
   southeastward-moving front this afternoon and evening, given a
   relatively moist and weakly unstable air mass. While 25-30-kt
   midlevel flow will conditionally support an isolated strong storm or
   two near the coast, the weak buoyancy will limit severe potential.

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0100Z

spc.summary: Isolated thunderstorms are possible over parts of western/southern Texas, the Gulf Coast, Florida, and the West Coast Tuesday. Severe storms are unlikely.
spc.text:
SPC AC 231731

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1131 AM CST Mon Nov 23 2026

   Valid 241200Z - 251200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated thunderstorms are possible over parts of western/southern
   Texas, the Gulf Coast, Florida, and the West Coast Tuesday. Severe
   storms are unlikely.

   ...South Florida/Keys...
   As the upper trough over Texas moves eastward and digs into the
   central Gulf, a surface low is expected to develop late Tuesday into
   Wednesday morning. This will eventually encourage the northward
   movement of a remnant surface boundary into the Florida Keys. Rich
   low-level moisture is present south of this boundary and at least
   modest--and increasing--deep-layer shear is expected. The main
   uncertainty is how far north this boundary advances. This is a
   low/conditional risk for stronger storms capable of strong gusts and
   potentially a waterspout. Confidence in severe risk still remains
   low, however.

   ...Lower Mississippi Valley...
   Weak, elevated buoyancy will during the evening into the overnight.
   Forcing for ascent from the approaching shortwave trough as well as
   low-level warm advection over a cool, stable surface layer will
   likely promote isolated thunderstorm development. Severe weather is
   not anticipated with this activity.

   ...Trans-Pecos/Central Texas/South Texas...
   Elevated thunderstorms along with isolated lightning flashes are
   possible early Tuesday in association with the southeastward digging
   shortwave trough. Limited buoyancy will preclude severe weather.

   ...Central/northern California Coast and Olympic Peninsula...
   A line of shallow convection, perhaps with isolated lightning, will
   approach the central/northern California coast during the afternoon
   as a weakening upper-level shortwave trough approaches. Buoyancy
   inland will be weak and lead to a rapid decrease in what will
   already be weak convection. A brief overlap of shallow buoyancy and
   enhanced flow in the lowest 3-4 km could promote stronger wind gusts
   along the immediate coast.

   Additional storms, perhaps a mix of linear/cellular structures are
   possible later in the evening near the Olympic Peninsula. Similar to
   farther south, buoyancy will be relatively shallow. Wind fields will
   be stronger, however. A few stronger gusts are possible, but
   organized severe weather is not expected given the limited buoyancy.

   ..Wendt.. 11/23/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 231924

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0124 PM CST Mon Nov 23 2026

   Valid 251200Z - 261200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF
   SOUTH FLORIDA AND THE FLORIDA KEYS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe storms are possible over parts of South
   Florida Wednesday.

   ...South Florida/Keys...
   The evolution of the upper trough within the northern/central Gulf
   differs between the GFS/ECMWF. This leads to variability in the
   track/intensity of the surface low that is expected to develop
   within the Florida Straits and move quickly northward along the East
   Coast into the Carolinas by Thursday morning. There is uncertainty
   as to how much warm sector will lift into the Keys/South Florida.
   The low-level environment within the warm sector, coupled with
   adequate deep-layer shear and modestly strong 850 mb flow, would
   support some storm organization with potential for isolated damaging
   winds and perhaps a tornado. This conditional threat would last
   through mid/late morning before 850 mb winds begin to veer. 

   ...Parts of Coastal Carolinas...
   The variability in the intensity/location of the surface low by
   early Thursday morning is quite large. The GFS shows a much deeper
   surface low than the ECMWF given a more focused/potent shortwave
   trough by Wednesday night into Thursday. Secondary to that, cool,
   dry continental air will be in place ahead of this surface low. The
   overall quality of moisture even with a more favorable track of the
   surface low also remains a question. Strong low-level wind fields
   would support some severe risk conditional on the degree of warm
   sector penetration inland. For now, severe potential is far to
   uncertain for probabilities.

   ..Wendt.. 11/23/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS03 PTSDY3 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0830Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
